source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"They regulate body temperature as efficiently as adults, so environmental exposure has little effect on their core temperature.","B":"Their normal temperature is always substantially lower than an adult's, making low readings expected in healthy infants.","C":"Their temperature should be interpreted with one fixed adult threshold regardless of age, measurement site, or clinical context.","D":"Their thermoregulation is less mature, so they can lose or gain heat rapidly and require age-appropriate temperature assessment."}}
source_row.rationale: Young infants have immature thermoregulation and physiologic features that increase susceptibility to temperature instability; temperature must be interpreted in age and measurement context.
